analysis: Scope: head-side test-only changes in provider-swift/Tests/ProviderCoreTests/KVCacheSSD/SSDPrefixCacheTests.swift (lines 610-1734 visible; the patch excerpt adds new whole-root maintainer tests around head lines ~3140-3240, which were truncated and not visible to me). No production source is changed in the supplied units. The visible tests assert behavior matching the T-041 posture: DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE kill switch (gateMatrix, lines 627-636), 30-minute TTL max that the env var can only shorten (lines 719-744), box-wide disk budget (683-717), verified non-empty weight hash binding (638-644), test-root isolation requiring the ephemeral-key gate (646-673), salt isolation (969-995), corruption leading to delete and recompute (997-1030), symlink-replacement not followed on reconcile, TTL, and eviction (1544-1654), epoch retention on eviction, TTL, and corruption (1223-1321), disowned-cache refusal to mutate after a binding change (1323-1366), and the write cap (1656-1704). These tests reinforce rather than weaken the T-041 mitigations. The tests do not alter the TTL ceiling, account scoping, name derivation, or kill-switch semantics. The characterization test at lines 1094-1167 documents that read eligibility depends on the sweep (stage can still hit an expired-but-unswept entry). It is explicitly labeled an existing sweep-enforced contract, not a change, and it falls within the accepted SEC-035 TTL window posture; I do not flag it as a regression. Open question for integration: the new maintainer verdict-caching tests (remembersHeaderVerdictsOnlyForUnchangedFiles, replacedLookalikeIsReadAgain) imply production changes to SSDWholeRootMaintainer, which are in other units and were not visible here. Reviewers should check ctime/size/mtime invalidation of cached ownership verdicts and symlink/no-follow handling there.
